title: Self-Healing Expression Evaluation via Balanced Operator Trees in Ruby
topic: The Self-Healing Code Thesis: Compilers, AI, and the Next 10 Years of Software
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a self-healing expression evaluator that transforms malformed arithmetic expressions into syntactically correct forms using a balanced operator tree. The evaluator is implemented in Ruby and integrates a lightweight parser, a shunting-yard conversion, and a recursive healing routine that preserves a strict height-balanced invariant. We formally prove that the tree remains height-balanced after each healing step, guaranteeing $O(\log n)$ search and update costs. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor with 1 physical core and 2 logical threads yields a mean latency of 103 076.44 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 9 702 ops/s over 30 iterations. This work demonstrates that compiler-level self-repair can be achieved without sacrificing performance. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/ruby-algorithms-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261024_130133_the_self-healing_code_thesis}
